top_choice_rationale: The optical lattice clock is a single, sharply defined invention: the magic-wavelength condition removes Doppler and recoil shifts while many atoms are interrogated at once, and the resulting accuracy near 1e-18 has been reproduced in several species and laboratories. The Katori and Ye allocation maps onto concept and first demonstration versus record accuracy and many-body clock physics, and a narrow citation on the lattice concept handles the overlap with the 2005 and 2012 prizes. I would still prefer this to no award, although its weight lies more in measurement capability than in new understanding of matter.
